text: Here's the one fact about a computer that changes how you think about all of this: a computer follows instructions literally and in order. It will not fill in the gaps, and it will not guess what you meant. If you leave a step out, it simply won't happen. That is exactly why programming exists — the computer supplies the speed, and you supply the thinking. So what does programming actually involve? Three moves, always in the same shape. First, understand the problem. Second, work out a solution — the plan. Third, write that plan as a sequence of clear instructions the computer can execute. That sequence is your program. And because the computer obeys in order, the order of the instructions is part of the meaning. The same steps in the wrong order can give the wrong result, or no result at all.
